messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/generate in us-west-2 routing -> signs of control-plane auth/config fetch backpressure. Auto-page to #incidents and on-call.

alex: seeing p95 ~1.2s -> p99 jump to ~5.6s over last 10m. Streaming stalls increasing, clients report partial streams. Logs show a few 429s from token-store and a lot of delayed config fetches.

sara: confirmed 429s from token-store (auth-db) + configstore timeouts. Snapshot from last 5m:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z INF token-lookup latency=120ms status=200
2026-03-15T14:02:18Z ERR token-validate status=429 detail="rate limit"
2026-03-15T14:03:02Z WARN config-fetch timeout=15000ms route=/v1/generate
```

mike: paging details look like a token-store auth rate-window burst + configstore fanout to featureflag service. Some calls block inference startup path (sync fetch). We have automatic fallback disabled for a recent rollout (featureflag:sync-config=true) — that could be why.

jess: tagging customer-impact. Early telemetry shows 0.8% of hosted API calls failing to complete streaming and ~3% higher tail latency for paying customers on standard tier. @support please gather any tickets.

alex: mitigation idea 1: flip featureflag sync-config to false (make fetch async+cached) to stop blocking. mitigation idea 2: temporarily broaden token-store rate limit for internal control-plane clients for next 15 minutes. mitigation idea 3: route new traffic to Dedicated pool if capacity available.

sara: can we do 1 quickly? It's a flag in controlplane-ff service. I can patch the flag via console or curl.

rick: I can do the flag flip and monitor. Command to flip (console UI preferred) but CLI available:
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/api/ff/patch -d '{"flag":"sync-config","value":false}'
```

deploy-bot: Canary deployment 2026-03-15T13:45:00 for controlplane-ff paused due to health check fails (not related). No active rollout in last 30m that touches sync-config.

mike: if we flip the flag, also temporarily enable local token caching at inference-sidecar (ttl 30s) to smooth auth calls. alex can you push a quick patch to sidecar config? small json patch should suffice.

alex: pushing patch to sidecar config now. Patch:
```
kubectl patch configmap inference-sidecar-config -n prod -p '{"data":{"token_cache_ttl":"30s"}}'
```

alex: restarted sidecars on a small canary subset (5 pods) `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-sidecar -n prod --selector=canary=true` — monitoring.

sara: token-store ops: raising temporary token service rate-limit per-client token bucket. ETA 2 mins. Running:
```
UPDATE rate_limits SET burst=500 WHERE service='controlplane' and client='inference';
```

sara: (2m) rate-limit change applied. metrics: auth 429s dropping from 12/min -> 0-1/min. configstore timeouts falling.

jess: customer impact note: drafting short status that latency spike is being mitigated; no evidence of data loss. Will post to status page if p99 remains <2s for 15m.

mike: keep the flag flip and sidecar cache until we confirm stability. plan to revert changes once root cause is fixed and we have a safer rollout for sync-config.

alex: p99 now down to 1.6s, streaming stalls reduced by ~70% in the canary region. Rolling sidecar restarts to remaining pods in waves.

rick: I'll take over monitoring and run a deeper postmortem. @oncall-bot note: handoff to next on-call in 30m. Actions for postmortem: capture configstore and token-store spike timelines, list deployments that depend on sync-config, and evaluate fallback behavior for streaming.

jess: noted. I will coordinate customer comms with SRE summary and estimated ETA to full remediation.

oncall-bot: REMINDER: on-call Handoff scheduled at 3098770321. Please escalate if p99 > 3s or error rate > 1% in next 30m. :bell:

alex: thanks team. leaving logs & traces link: https://observability.internal/trace/3098765432 — capture any additional anomalies there."
